whatIs.title: What is BrightBoost?
whatIs.body: BrightBoost is a bilingual (English/Spanish) K-8 STEM learning platform that builds strong foundations and prepares students for advanced technology pathways in AI, quantum, and biotech. The platform features tiered pathways for K-2, 3-5, and 6-8. The current rollout begins with K-2 content — turning foundational skills like sequencing, patterns, and problem-solving into interactive game-based adventures. Teachers create classes, assign modules, and track student progress. Students play through activities, earn XP, and build confidence. Grades 3-5 and 6-8 are planned in future releases.

explore.step1Desc: A ready-made presentation showing what students learn, sample achievements, and family take-home activities. No login required.
explore.step2Desc: Log in with the demo teacher account to see class management, resources, the prep checklist, and the PD Hub.

lookFor.title: What to Look For as a Partner
lookFor.intro: As you explore, here are four lenses that help evaluate BrightBoost for your context:
lookFor.engagementDesc: Are the current K-2 activities age-appropriate and motivating? Does the XP/avatar system feel rewarding? Can you see this scaling to 3-5 and 6-8?
lookFor.teacherUxDesc: Is it easy to create a class, assign work, and check progress? Does the prep checklist help with lesson planning?
lookFor.accessibilityDesc: Does the icon-based login work for pre-readers? Is the bilingual support effective? Does it load on Chromebooks?
lookFor.trustDesc: Is it clear what data is collected? Does the privacy policy address your concerns? Is the audit trail visible?

privacy.title: Privacy & Trust
privacy.item1: BrightBoost collects only learning progress data — no ads, no third-party tracking
privacy.item2: COPPA-aware design: early learner accounts (K-2) don't require email or passwords
privacy.item3: All data can be exported or deleted at the end of a pilot
privacy.item4: Audit logging tracks login, signup, and password reset events

help.title: How to play
help.step1: Tap a part, then tap the land to build it.
help.step2: Press the green "Let it flow!" to run the water.
help.step3: Try "Rain" — does your river still work?
help.note: There's no wrong way — just build and watch! 🌊

fishmouth.what: At Dujiangyan, a long stone island shaped like a fish's mouth sits in the middle of the Min River.
fishmouth.built: Li Bing built it 2,300 years ago to split one wild river into two calmer ones — no dam, just clever shape.
fishmouth.river: In your river, the Fish Mouth splits the water two ways — dig channels above and below it!

sandweir.what: The Flying Sand Weir is a low spillway that lets floodwater and sand escape over its edge.
sandweir.built: Li Bing made it just low enough: normal water flows past, but flood water spills safely away.
sandweir.river: In your river, the Sand Weir spills extra water off the map — watch the 💦 when a flood hits it!

bottleneck.what: The Bottle-Neck is a narrow gap Li Bing's team cut through a whole mountain of rock.
bottleneck.built: It took 8 years of heating the rock with fire and cooling it with water to crack it open — no explosives existed!
bottleneck.river: In your river, the Bottle-Neck lets only a gentle flow through, so your fields drink without drowning.

parents.title: For Parents & Families
parents.subtitle: Bright Boost is a multilingual STEM learning platform for kids — built for classrooms, after-school programs, and home.

classroom.title: In the classroom
classroom.desc: Teachers run sessions and see each child's progress.

afterschool.title: After school
afterschool.desc: Program leaders use the same activities with small groups.

home.title: At home
home.desc: Families explore together — or kids explore on their own.

journey.title: How the learning is organized
journey.intro: Children move through three sets of activities. Each one builds on the last.

stages.foundationDesc: Structured, highly supported introductions to STEM ideas. Every activity guides children step by step.
stages.explorationDesc: Children predict, plan, test, measure, and revise — with more room to make their own choices.
stages.masteryDesc: Creation-first experiences built around Imagine → Create → Play → Share → Reflect. Children make things of their own.

role.title: Your role: a guide, not a proctor
role.p1: Kids do best when a nearby adult is curious with them — not checking their answers.
role.b1: Ask what they notice and what they want to try.
role.b2: Help with reading only when they ask.
role.b3: Let them experiment — unexpected results are part of the learning.
role.b4: Children can also explore entirely on their own.

guideCard.title: K–2 Facilitator Quick Start
guideCard.desc: A one-page printable guide for any adult sitting alongside a young learner.

parentGuide.docTitle: K–2 Facilitator Quick Start — Bright Boost
parentGuide.title: K–2 Facilitator Quick Start
parentGuide.subtitle: For any adult alongside a young learner — parents, tutors, program leaders, and teachers.
parentGuide.teacherCardDesc: Printable one-pager for parents and program volunteers — before, during, and after an activity.

before.title: Before you start (2 minutes)
before.b1: Open the activity once yourself so you know what the child will see.
before.b2: Check the device: charged, connected, sound on if you have it.
before.b3: Invite curiosity: "We get to try something new today."

during.title: While they play
during.b1: Help with reading only when the child asks or gets stuck.
during.b2: Ask wondering questions instead of giving answers.
during.b3: Encourage experimenting — trying, changing, and even "breaking" things is how the games are meant to be played.
during.b4: If they ask you for the answer, try: "What could we try to find out?"

after.title: Afterwards
after.b1: Ask what they noticed and what surprised them.
after.b2: Ask what they changed, made, or figured out.
after.b3: Ask what they want to try next time.

prompts.title: Prompts you can use as-is
prompts.p2: What do you think will happen if…?
prompts.p3: How did you figure that out?
prompts.p4: What would you change next time?
prompts.p5: Can you show me what you made?
prompts.p7: What do you want to try next?

parentGuide.independence: You don't have to be there the whole time. The activities are built so a child can explore on their own — your curiosity is a bonus, not a requirement.
